cases.adjudication: Author-acknowledged coding error; material magnitude correction without reversal. First public disclosure unresolved.
cases.mechanism: An unrecognized TAXSIM v8-to-v9 change made variable v28 federal tax before rather than after credits; the original after-tax family-income measure omitted EITC payments.
cases.consequence: Author correction Table 3: combined math/reading income coefficient 0.0411 SD per $1,000 (SE 0.0131), versus about 0.06 originally. Reply says approximately 30% smaller IV estimates and almost 40% larger first stage; reduced form and statistical significance unchanged. Published comment abstract says 32% smaller.
cases.correction_only: The main income coding correction rescales first stage and IV. Corrected tables also incorporate minor state-credit and EITC-schedule corrections (footnote 3), so table values should not be represented as isolating exactly one change.
cases.response_status: Dahl and Lochner explicitly acknowledge the coding error and thank Lundstrom. They defend substantive income effects and address a separate sample-period robustness critique.

cases.adjudication: Substantive candidate, but mechanism not conclusively traced; keep missing-data discrepancy separate from functional-form dispute.
cases.mechanism: Report infers nonresponse codes may have been treated as values, e.g. unknown revenue 88,888,888,888. Even implementing that presumed mistake does not reproduce original sample sizes. Authors explicitly cannot determine exact discrepancy causes; reporting errors are another possibility.
cases.consequence: Reported original seven of eight positive p<.05 associations become three of eight in the replication using proper missing-value exclusions, all still positive. Additional logarithmic transformations leave one of eight. Full-model sample sizes 239/270/348/362 compared with original 506/506/469/484 for revenue/customers/market-share/profitability.
cases.correction_only: Three of eight is the missing-data-only replication result, but because original computation is not reconstructed it is not an isolated code-patch counterfactual. One of eight additionally changes outcome/control functional forms and must not be attributed wholly to established mistakes.
cases.response_status: Herring reply publisher abstract defends updated evidence linking diversity and business success. Full reply not recovered (publisher blocked); cannot classify whether missing-code hypothesis is conceded or how it is rebutted.

cases.adjudication: Author-acknowledged coding mistakes materially affect one negative-binomial patent robustness check. Broader conclusions disputed; earliest public date incompletely resolved.
cases.mechanism: Negative-binomial model used patents+1 instead of raw counts and separate country/year fixed effects instead of country-by-year effects. Comment also drops industry effects to match written equation; reply disputes dropping those effects.
cases.consequence: Reply Table 1 original 0.398 (SE 0.168), corrected counts and country-by-year FE 0.116 (0.490). Correcting dependent variable alone in comment gives -0.15 (0.47). Further dropping industry FE gives -0.73 (0.34), but that additional choice is disputed. All use 74,038 observations. Reply adding initial Chinese import exposure yields 1.089 (0.575), p<.10, with further variants significant at .05/.01.
cases.correction_only: Use 0.398 to 0.116 as agreed coding correction; do not use the negative estimate after disputed FE removal as agreed correction. Changes to log(1+patents) elsewhere concern modeling/estimand and trends. The coding result is a robustness-specification finding, not proof all original innovation, IT and productivity findings reverse.
cases.response_status: Reply acknowledges errors but defends industry FE and argues initial-condition controls restore positive results. This defense uses additional controls beyond the simple coding correction.

cases.adjudication: Full report documents concrete SD/SE and data-entry issues and an important changed take-option result; correction bundle also changes censoring/definition. Material impact of hard mistakes alone not isolated.
cases.mechanism: For List aggregate data, SDs used instead of SEs, underweighting study. Some negative-mean treatments omitted; Bardsley participant counts mistaken across treatments; negative giving truncated to zero in aggregate and excluded from individual data. These issues have different epistemic status: SD/SE and transcription are computational/data errors; censoring and comparable-giving definitions require substantive assessment.
cases.consequence: 2012 working-paper Table 6 take-option meta-regression coefficient -0.331 (p<.001), OLS -0.428 (p<.001), treatment FE -0.272 (p<.001), Tobit -0.362 (p<.001); original take-option estimates nonsignificant. Final 2014 comment reports a different meta coefficient (-0.603) after broader recoding; do not interchange versions. Most other findings described as robust.
cases.correction_only: The displayed consequence follows bundled recoding/reinstatement of negative giving and hard data errors. A hard-errors-only correction is not reported in the inspected full 2012 paper. Separate normalized-giving analyses alter the outcome reference point further.
cases.response_status: No formal Engel response located. Comment acknowledges Engel supplied data and answered questions; that does not establish agreement with all criticisms.
